technical_facts: Research into lummigraphs (digital holograms) revealed immense space requirements (several gigabytes uncompressed for a single room).
Proposed 'lumigraphlets' as view-dependent texture imposters for large clusters of areas.
Explored extending Quake 2 sky box rendering into a full system using interpolation between up to four environment map snapshots in a tetrahedral arrangement.
Determined that simple image-based interpolation between environment maps causes 'ghosting' and lacks a sense of motion.
Discovered that adding depth values to environment map cubes allows rendering as small triangles at world coordinates, enabling movement within a map and better blending.
Identified texture smearing during occlusion reveals and blurring when moving far from the camera point as drawbacks of the depth-mapped environment map approach.
Noted that low-res environment maps (700k per snapshot) would generate too excessive data if used throughout a level.
Proposed a fractal compression method for environment maps using projective maps to handle redundant surface images across multiple snapshots.
Identified a connection between lummigraphs, environment maps, specularity, convolution, and dynamic indirect lighting.
personality_patterns: Willingness to engage in 'wide open research' for months without a guaranteed outcome.
Acceptance of failure in early research directions; views learning as a long-term payoff ('Ah well, I learned a lot').
Analytical approach to identifying the specific failures of a technology (e.g., ghosting, memory requirements, 'silhouette crease' in depth data).
Intellectual curiosity and naggingging interest in unsolved problems ('Its nagging at me, but it hasn't come completely clear').
Critical view of hardware-suggested bump mapping approaches, labeling them as 'bogus'.

gnosis_principles.description: Allowing periods of open-ended research to explore potential technologies, accepting that not all paths will lead to the final implementation, but the cumulative knowledge gained is valuable.
The goal of creating rendering techniques that are completely complexity insensitive, meaning performance remains stable regardless of the scene's geometric complexity.

Identifying redundancies in image-based rendering (e.g., the same wall appearing in multiple snapshots) and seeking mathematical transformations (like projective maps) to compress the data efficiently.

heritage_patterns: Iterative refinement of existing engine technology (extending Quake 2 sky box logic to a full rendering system).
Focus on high-performance, id Software-style optimization of memory and memory bandwidth (addressing the 'immense' space requirements of lummigraphs).
Preference for first-person shooter (FPS) suitability over general-purpose rendering techniques.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What happened to the research John Carmack did at the start of the Quake 3 development?
dpo_pairs.chosen: Carmack spent a few months of wide open research that ultimately had no bearing on the directions he finally decided on for the Quake 3/trinity engine, though he viewed the learning experience as a valuable long-term investment.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He used the research to build the core of the Quake 3 engine.
